Container.Name: Headroom
Container.Overview:
A household budget web app and PWA. Shows the chequing balance, how much is safe to spend before the next bill, every upcoming paycheque and bill with a running balance, two-week pay periods, the monthly budget, savings and the mortgage payoff outlook.
THREE VARIABLES ARE REQUIRED and the container will refuse to start without them: APP_ORIGIN, DATABASE_URL and SESSION_SECRET. Everything else has a sensible default.
BEFORE FIRST START, create the database on your PostgreSQL 17 server: CREATE DATABASE headroom; The container creates its own tables on every start, but it does not create the database.
NO APPDATA PATH IS NEEDED. Everything lives in PostgreSQL, so there is no volume to map and nothing to back up on the Unraid side. Back up the database instead: scripts/backup.mjs in the repository does a dump and proves it restores.
NO WEBUI LINK ON PURPOSE. The session cookie is HTTPS-only, so opening the app at http://server-ip:port shows the interface and then silently fails to sign you in. Open it at the HTTPS address you put in APP_ORIGIN, through a reverse proxy. docs/DEPLOY.md has the Nginx Proxy Manager settings, including the two headers Server-Sent Events needs.
AFTER FIRST START, create the two accounts from the Unraid terminal: docker exec -it Headroom node apps/api/dist/cli.js create-user Run it twice. The first account also creates the household; the second joins it.
Container.Requires: A PostgreSQL 17 server reachable from this container, and an empty database on it.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Host port the reverse proxy forwards to. The container always listens on 3000.

Config.Name: APP_ORIGIN
Config.Description: REQUIRED. The exact address you open the app at, including https:// and no trailing slash, e.g. https://headroom.example.com. Cookies and CORS are checked against it, so a mismatch shows up as a login that appears to work and then forgets you.

Config.Name: DATABASE_URL
Config.Description: REQUIRED. Connection string for your PostgreSQL 17 server, e.g. postgresql://headroom:PASSWORD@192.168.1.50:5432/headroom?schema=public . The user needs rights to create tables, types and triggers. Create the database itself first; the container does not.

Config.Name: SESSION_SECRET
Config.Description: REQUIRED. At least 32 characters, used to sign the session cookie. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 32 . Changing it signs everyone out.

Config.Name: TZ
Config.Description: Optional. The server clock decides every date the app stores, so this should be the household's own timezone. America/Regina has no daylight saving.

Config.Name: COOKIE_SECURE
Config.Description: Optional, defaults to true. Leave it true: the session cookie then travels only over HTTPS. Setting it false is for plain-http development and should never be used with real data.

Config.Name: LOG_LEVEL
Config.Description: Optional, defaults to info. One of fatal, error, warn, info, debug, trace, silent. Use debug while something is wrong.

Config.Name: SESSION_TTL_DAYS
Config.Description: Optional, defaults to 90. How long a sign-in lasts. Long on purpose, because the app is opened many times a day. 1 to 400.

Config.Name: LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT
Config.Description: Optional, defaults to 10. FAILED sign-in attempts allowed per address per 15 minutes. Successful sign-ins are not limited.

Config.Name: IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_TTL_HOURS
Config.Description: Optional, defaults to 48. How long the server remembers a write's idempotency key, so a retry from a phone on a weak connection cannot apply the same change twice.

Config.Name: SSE_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS
Config.Description: Optional, defaults to 25. Keep-alive interval for the live-update stream that refreshes the other phone. Lower it if a proxy closes idle connections sooner than this.

Config.Name: VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY
Config.Description: Optional and not used yet; push notifications are a later milestone. Generate all three VAPID values together with: npx web-push generate-vapid-keys . Either set all three or leave all three empty.

Config.Name: VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY
Config.Description: Optional and not used yet. The private half of the VAPID pair above.

Config.Name: VAPID_SUBJECT
Config.Description: Optional and not used yet. A contact address for the push service, e.g. mailto:admin@example.com
